case_title: Budhi Singh v. State of H.P.
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 IPC, sentenced to life imprisonment
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
neutral_facts: The accused, who was the brother of the deceased, was involved in an incident where the deceased, who was drunk, abused and assaulted his father. The father called for help, and the accused came out with a tobru (small axe) and struck the deceased on the head, resulting in fatal injuries. The deceased's injuries were severe, leading to his death. The prosecution argued that the accused had inflicted the fatal injuries, and the trial court convicted the accused under Section 302 of the IPC. The High Court affirmed the conviction. The Supreme Court considered whether the offence fell under Section 302 or 304 IPC, noting that the deceased's actions were a sudden and grave provocation, leading to the conclusion that the accused's actions were not premeditated and did not amount to murder. The accused was therefore convicted under Section 304 (Part I) IPC and sentenced to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 5,000.
